claims.statement: Both cloud and local Copilot sandboxes are described as public-preview and subject to change. This broader note includes cloud as well as local scope, but proves neither enabled isolation, availability, safe execution nor a cost grant.

Continuing or resuming a CLI session that previously had remote control enabled automatically reenables remote control. Prior session state therefore matters; resume must not be assumed local-only. The fragment does not establish authentication, connection recipients, consent freshness or actual remote control here; neither example was executed.

The pinned remote-interface note says slash commands such as allow-all are unavailable there at that snapshot. An interface limitation is not proof that every approval bypass is impossible, equivalent local/remote capabilities or verified permission enforcement.

Windows local sandboxing requires a Windows Insiders build according to the pinned prerequisite. Presence of that build alone does not prove sandbox availability or isolation; this is not an instruction to enroll or change the operating system.

The contextless fragment lists touch, chmod, node and sed as examples associated with tools needing approval. It does not supply a complete command policy, action-specific authorization or proof that other commands are safe; read/write behavior depends on actual invocation and parent context remains separate.
